cells.place: On the wall of Kalāhastīśvara temple †
cells.date: 28th year [date-calculation appendix, No. 83: Uttarāyaṇa-Sankramaṇa in A. D. 1139-40 (= Siddhārthi) fell on Monday 25th December 1139 which was Pausha śukla 3, not Mārgaśīra śukla 5. Mārgaśīra śu. 5 cannot join with Uttarāyaṇa-Sańkramaṇa, because Mārgaśīra even in a year in which it is preceded by an adhika month cannot begin after the 266th day of the Solar year and the 5th tithi of Mārgaśīra can therefore never take us beyond the 271st day of the Solar year, whereas Uttarāyaṇa-Sańkramaṇa must fall on the 275th or 276th day.]

14th [date-calculation appendix, No. 128: 15th year. Pramōda, Āśvayuja, Amāvāsyā, eclipse. The solar eclipse was in
Kārttika month, (not in Āśvina month) i.e., Sunday 24 Nov. A.D. 1090.
17th year. Āngirasa śu. 3 Monday = A.D. 1092, Monday 12th April.
50th year. Viśvāvasu—Bānada Punnamē, Monday. It is stated in the Tables
of Calculation published by the Basel Mission Tract Depository that the full
moon day of the month of Pushya is called Bānada punnamē. The only
paurnamīs which in A.D. 1125-26 (= Viśvāvasu) fell Monday were (1)
Āśvina full moon, Monday, September 14·58, A.D. 1125 ... (2) the full moon
in the Solar month of Pushya (Tamil Tai = Makara) which ended on Monday,
11th January, A.D. 1126, very shortly after sunrise : the lunar month was
Māgha, not Pausha. If the paurnamī in question is regulated by the solar
month of Pushya, the second of these dates must be the one intended in the
inscription.]

cells.place: On the fourth viragal in the place of Siddhēśvara temple .. †
cells.remarks: Registers a hypothecation deed in which the parties were a certain Savarṇi Dāvan, king Karunāṭa-Rāma Rāma-Ravivarmman, Koḷattu Tiruvadi and the feudatories of Perumchehallur. Unfinished. It is written in the beginning, in the middle and perhaps also in the end. The Tamil portion of the record mentions the grant of the village, Dāyanātha. 308 Brahmans at the instance of the chief Dāyanātha. The Tamil portion, of which much has been lost, mentions the gift of land to the temple of Tiruvāñjikkuḷam by the king. The Teyk-rai-Nāyir-nuḍu of Śōḷa-nāḍu. It was perhaps this land that was granted under the name Dāyanātham-galam.

cells.location: TIRUNAGESVARAM
cells.place: On the north wall of Kuntavai temple †
cells.remarks: Partly damaged and built in. Registers the jewels, gold and silver vessels, etc., owned by the temple, with the permission of the king which was obtained at the request of [the temple] servant named Kaṇḍan Kōvalanāṇ. Tirungāṇīśvaramuḍaiyār-nāyanār, the deity to whom it is situated in Tirukkudamukkil in Pauhur-nādu, a sub-division of Jayakoṇḍasōḷa-vaḷanādu. Records that the assembly (uḷḷa-parid-uṛuar) of Tirukkudamukkil receive 100 kaḷañju from Maṇikkan Māvali alias Vikkiramaśiṅga-Pallavaraiyan, a native of Mērundam in Viṅkuṇṛa-kōṭṭam, a sub-division of Jayakoṇḍasōḷa-maṇḍalam. This money was deposited by them for repairing damages caused by floods to the irrigation channel. Inter alia, it states that out of the interest on each kaḷañju was set apart for providing offerings in the temple of Tirungāḻavam-Uḍaiyār and for expounding the Sivadharma in the assembly hall called Toʻuṉchiyurrambalamayiṉ built in the temple by the above-mentioned Vikkiramaśiṅga-Pallavarai-yan.

cells.location: TIRUNAGESVARAM
cells.place: On the same wall
cells.remarks: Sale of 1/2 vēli of land to the same temple by the assembly of Madamaṅgalam a brāhmaṇa [dēvadāna] in Tiruṇāṟaiyur-nādu. Tiruviņṇagar-Tiruvāṇaivaraṇ is stated to have been a dēvadāna in Tirunaṛ-nādu. The cost of the land viz. 101 kaḷañju, 6mañji and 1/2 mañjāḍi was formerly deposited for offerings by the princess Aruḷmoli-Piṅgai, who was the Bāṇa queen and daughter of prince Arikulakēsari. An introductory Praśasti beginning with singulur taru is inscribed next to this, but is much damaged and incomplete.

Śaka Vikriti. [date-calculation appendix, No. 386: [5]th year. A.D. 1267, Saturday, August 18 ; f.d.t. •07; •28.

August 1913, quoted above.]

Śaka 1155, Nandana. [date-calculation appendix, No. 448: 13th year of (?) See paragraph 19 of Part II of the Report. The eclipse was
presumably one coinciding with Nak. Pūrva-Bhādrapadā. The indication
is that of a solar eclipse. Such a coincidence can only take place at the end
of ordinary lunar Māgha; while a coincidence of Nak. Pūr.-Bhādrapadā with
a lunar eclipse can take place in ordinary lunar Āśvina. It is curious that a
coincidence of each of the two kinds took place in the 13th year of one Pāndya,
viz., Māyāvarman Kulasekhara. The first kind of coincidence took place in
A.D. 1281, Thursday, February 20; •34; •75. The second kind of coincidence
took place in A.D. 1280 on Monday, September 9 ; f.d.t., •38 ; •73.]

cells.remarks: Built in at the beginning. Gift of land (madē tax free) to a certain Kaṇavāniya Perumāļāļvar, by a native of Kari(n)t-ai in Pāṇḍya Vinnagarālu at Ten Tiruvāytōrai. The document is signed by a number of officers in 'the department of taxes.' cells.place: On the wall of Viśvanāthasvāmin temple †
cells.remarks: Gift of money for two lamps in the temple of Tirunelvēliyuda-yār by Bêjjâ-Kamma, the brother-in-law of Danndâ-nāyaka the danlânâyaka of the king Virapratâpa-Sômadêva. Much damaged. Gift by Virapra-Nāyaka for the merit of his father Krishnappa-Nayaka of the Kaśyapa-gōtra, to the temple of Tiruvâgadanâthana at Krishnâpuram on the bank of the Tâmaraparni (river). Mentions the Tirurudi country (Sêlam). Regard-ing certain Ariyankûttan, Puttânâri alias Tiruvêngadanâ-nāllur, Pottakkîrattân alias Krishnan, Kulôttunga-chôla-brahma-rayan, and some land in Alikudi to the temple of Tiruvangadanâ-dēva by Krishnappa-Nâyaka, for the merit of his father Viśva-nâtha-Nayaka of the Kasyapa-gōtra. It is stated that the latter had acquired the iraiyidias in which these villages were sit-uated. Mentions Amara[vu]ndâya-Nāyan.

cells.remarks: This inscription was partially copied in 1902. Registers that the land given for service of Subramanya-Bhatara provided 1,400 kalam of paddy (kâdu) for 12 months of the year. The money was distributed among 16 villages which were required only to pay interest at 2 kalam of paddy per year on each kasu borrowed, without disturbing the principal.

cells.place: On a viragal set up on the 'south-east side of Chalukya temple. †
cells.king: Yara-Timmaraju, brother-in-law of Mahādēvarāya, ruling at Vijayanagara.
cells.remarks: The boundaries of the village Kēnnūru which was a surname of Tiruvenkaṇallūr in Gatti-rājya, are first described. Then follow details of mēra, mirāsi and other members and grantees, also village servants. This record pretends to belong to the reign of Praudhadeva-Mahārāja (Śaka 1371 to 1387). Incomplete. The genealogy of the Karata kings which the inscription begins, is identical with that given in the Kalkūruki grant of Sāṇiga VI, as far as Venkaṭa II. (See seal below inscription No. 115).'

cells.remarks: A plain forgery which professes to have been executed in the reign of Vijaya-Bukkabhūpa (Śaka 1381 to 1344). Registers the advent of a number of gauṇḍas from Nagara-sīma with their carts (i.e., baggago?), to settle in the country ruled by Sōmanśkara-Nāyaka of Ratnagiri. These new villages were founded and village officers appointed. Also mentions Malikiharbāra-varāha (i.e., pagoda issued by the Golconda king Malik Ibrāhim).

cells.place: On the wall of Addhiparēśvara temple †
cells.remarks: Registers a sale of land by the assembly of the Brahmanī-mahājana of Sundaraōāṭa-chaturvēdimanga-lam and Vāōgavāmahādēvi-chaturvēdimangalam. It was purchased by Nāgalvarvāhūbhaṇi alias Ariyammai wife of Prabhākara-Bhaṭṭa resident of Tiruvorriyūr, for the daily worship of the devotees of the temple of Tiruvorriyūrudāya-Mahādēva. The purchased land was given to the mahaṅādaṭa Rājendrasōlān which was built by that lady. Records also other sales of land to that temple and for the maintenance of the residents of Enur in Navalār-nādu which was a sub-division of Palār-kōṭu and by the merchants (nagarattār) of Tiru-vorriyūr in the years 31 and 27 of the same reign, respectively.

cells.remarks: Records that the firumānḍal-kēṭṭaikkāni was granted to Timmu-Nāyaka son of Pāmu-Nāyaka of Śātirapaḍi in Kalavai-paṛṛu, who recommended Āpattu-Nāyaka, Vēṅkaṭādri-Nāyaka and Pōttu-Nāyaka. cells.location: Lēpākshi
cells.place: On the wall of Nirvānar shrine †
cells.date: Śaka 1469, Hēmalambi, Jyeishtha, ba. di. 2, Thursday (=Feb. 21, A.D. 1588).
cells.remarks: Damaged. Records a gift to the shrines of Pāparāmisvadēva, Raghunāthadēva and Vīranārāyana, by Mādalūru Raghunāthayyan, son of Kāri Mada-samudra-agrahāra, a village in Rodd-nādu which was a sub-division of Penugonda-rājya. The gift consisted of a palaparis-channel below the tank of Amgapalli village, otherwise called Gulisettikunte in Addaganjali village. Mention is made of Ramayyan, brother of Penugonda Virappayya who was the son of Nandi-Lakinsetti of Lēpākshi.

cells.remarks: Records a sale of land to the same three shrines by the mahājunas of the Sarasandha-agrahāra, being Kaifatiyendra alias Pratāpasēvayāpura in Penugonda-rājya, belonging to the gift of Achyutadēva-Maharāya, when He made the grant gifts named kāmāthana, kalpavriksha and vīrachakra in the presence of the god Virupaksha on the banks of the Tungabhārā river. cells.remarks: Damaged. Gift of the village of Chaluvidla sur- named Komāra-Venkkaṭādripuram, to the temple of Papavināsanadēva at Lēpakshi. Much damaged. Gives the usual long genealogy commencing with the Moon. The remaining lines on the copper-plate doon that what follows is a copy of the copper-plate dona- ment of Vīrēsarandēva. After the long genealogy which is identically the same as that of the Una- mañjari plates it is recorded that the king weighed himself against gold at the same Śiva shrine in Saka 1465, Nandana and that he made the gift called Keshānamūru in Śāka 1465 [8], Vijaya. (Gift of tolls by the merchants of all countries headed by Prithvīvīchī Rayana-Bhāskara, to the temple of Śanta-Nañjunādēśvara at Lēpakehi.

cells.remarks: Registers that a document connected with the temple of Tiruvīraṭṭānamuḍaiyār-Uḍaiyār at Tirukkuppāpuram a brāhmaṇīya village of Marugal-nāḍu in Gēyamāṇikka-vaḷanāḍu, was engraved on the walls of the temple at Tiruchchengāṭṭanguḍi, as the temple of Tirukkuppāpuram was destroyed by a storm. The record refers to the 5th and 10th years of Periyadēvar Kuḷōttunga-Chōḷadēva in whose time the Tirukkuppāpuram temple came into existence.

cells.place: On another pillar in the place of Mallikārjuna temple †
cells.king: Vīrapratāpa Vīra Sadāśivarāya-Mahārāya, ruling at Vidyānagara.
cells.date: Śaka 1478, Parīdhāvi, vai. di. 3. Pramāthi, māgha, śu. di. 1, Monday,
cells.remarks: Records that works were constructed on this day. In insight different sets of the stone are given the names of eight persons whom perhaps the image represent. Some of these were Chandrabhāṭha and Mūlasangha and Chandra-dra, Badayya and Taṇṇamappa of the Apantiya (i.e. Āpastamba)-sūtra. The same individual also repaired a well and a lamp-pillar to the temple of Junbunāthadēva of that village.

cells.place: On the third pillar lying in the place of Mallikārjuna temple. †
cells.date: Śaka 1277, Pramādi, Jyēshṭha, śu., śu. di. 12.
cells.remarks: Damaged. Records that a Jaina merchant named Bhōgarāja consecrated the image of Śāntanātha- Jinēśvara rā. This merchant is stated to have been a pupil of Maṅgāpanandiviratin, the disciple of Abhayakīrtimuni, of Pustakasagachchha, dēśiya-gaṇa and Mala-vargu. Gift of the village Viṭhalāshpura by Tammamarāya, son of the Mahā-Nāyakāchārya Buṭṭuka Erapa-Nāyaka of Rayaduru, for the worship of the Jhana-sthana of his mother Peṇṇavva-Nakti (i.e. Nāyakitti).

cells.remarks: Mentions [Kōti] Bėta-Maharāya (also called Maitrāvarāya) founded the temple of Uttarēśvara with the shrine (Śankarēśvara), bull, flagstaff, minor deities, Vīrabhava (i.e., Vīrabhadra) and Kāļikā. He is further stated to have built the wall attached to the temple and the garden and granted land to the temple and to the priest for the worship of the linga and distribution of food in charity. He was the successor in Pūśapāti-Śamkhēvadbūthi of Śaṁkaraguru who attained Siva-boot, on the given date and had received the great penance of [his teacher] Munirantimandiguru.

cells.place: On a slab set up in the tank at Ilaparu (same taluk and district).
cells.remarks: Registers that while the chief minister Mummadi Bhaṭṭa was governing the sovereign country including Kuḍuravalli and other places, he constructed a tank on the south side of Panya. cells.place: On the rock below the dhvajastambha in the Chauḍēśvarī temple in the same village.
cells.date: Śaka 1508, Vyaya, Bhādra-pada, śu. di. 12, Sunday.
cells.remarks: Registers that Daḷavāyi Veṅkaṭa[ppa]-Nāyuḍu conveyed the dēvadāya and brāhmadāya lands below the tank of Hosakere, included in Penugoṇḍa, a district of Yerama[rāj]-rājya. These had been so enjoyed since the time of Chikka-Oḍaya but had been assessed in corn in some way and this distinction was made in the grant. The grant was made on the occasion when the king performed the Lakshahōma ceremony at Varadāraja-pēṭe. The stone was put up by Koṇḍaya under orders of Timmarasa at the elephant-sluco (?).

cells.place: On a slab near a tank in the same village (as Rāmasvāmin temple) †
cells.date: Śaka 1455, Vijaya, Phālguna, śu. di. 15, Saturday.
cells.remarks: Damaged at the beginning. Registers that the dēvadāya and brāhmadāya lands under the tank Kroṭṭacheruvu in Penugoṇḍa-rājya which had been held rent-free (sarvamānya) from the time of Chikka-Oḍaya had been re-assessed on account of some confusion in the state business orders and now at Sivanasamudram on state business orders that the lands might be restored as before and this was announced on the occasion of the Lakshahōma ceremony conducted at Penugoṇḍa. Kaṇama-Nāyuḍu had this inscription engraved under orders of Rāyasam Koṇḍamarusayya.

cells.remarks: The four pillars on the east side of this platform were the gift of Tirupati-vāru. Rātu-Sari Bhushana Pait, a, whom this record mentions as the builder of the temple in this translation is "Hundred Samvat Kuṇyā, 18th day" and believes that "the temple was constructed or dedicated to Tiruvidhēvarasvāmin" on this day. This is not likely; for the characters appear to be more modern.

cells.place: On a slab set up in the north of the same village (as Rāmasvāmin temple) to Kondapalli from the same village (as Rāmasvāmin temple). †
cells.remarks: Refers to general of the king, called Śaika Saharalli of Gujapati throne, who is the commander of the 84 forts of the Andhra Tri-liṅga (country). Mention is also made of the usurpation of the Gujapati throne by Siṅga of the Bahubalēndra family. A tank on the west bank of the Āśīka-Laṅgula (i.e., the river Laṅgulya flowing close by Āśka) called Siṅgasagaram was constructed by the Muḥammudan ohi-ul-Saha evidently in honour of the usurper Siṅga (Narasimha). Seems to mention the names of persons who had the image [of Vinayaka] out out the cross-beam.

cells.place: On a rock in a field at Nolamballi ('Punganur Zamindari, Chittoor district).
cells.remarks: Registers, that while the king was encamped at Vevīrrujnporone in Perjvi-nāļu he conferred with those of the inter, that lands declared to be superior to the eighth class as determined by Par- bīrja-lingānga (in the ashtabhamgaram) and those below the eighth class be allowed to con- tinue as before and that the site of the temple of Tiruttampgai-Iśvaran, its enclosure, premises and the sacred tank till now included in the tax-free land should pay no taxes to the state. The order was executed by the 'land- survey committee (nilam-ala-vagupa-pperumakkal) of the village assembly of Perumalappuriyūr. Full details of the lands (extent, boundaries, etc.) thus dealt with are recorded.

cells.remarks: Records that a gift of land for a flower-garden called Ponnambalakkūram, in the village of Koyilppadi, a hamiet of Perunagarppuliyūr, was made to the temple of Alagiyār by a certain [O]mpuli[yā]r, the younger brother of Arūndaiyār. The land was made tax-free. It was also provided for its upkeep by another gift of land made at Sērundi-ma[ṅg]alam, which was a hamlet of Tyāgavali-chaturvēdimangalam in Vērkā-nādu. These transactions and gifts were engraved on the walls of the temple by the order of the king's officer at the temple of Nārāyaṇa.
